Crude Futures End Little Changed

1540 ET – Oil futures settle near flat in a choppy trading session as continuing tensions in the Middle East are countered by improving supply. “The oil market has become acclimated to periodic flare-ups, just as long as there is no return to all-out war,” says Raymond James investment strategist Pavel Molchanov. “With oil production among OPEC’s Persian Gulf members having reached 87% of pre-war levels, the industry is gradually adapting.” WTI slips 0.1% to $83.21 ahead of Friday’s December contract expiry. Brent for January delivery edges up 3 cents to $91.98 a barrel. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

Oil Edges Higher But Surplus Expectations, U.S. Inventory Build Pressure Prices

0934 GMT – Oil prices tick higher as the market weighs expectations of a surplus against continued threats to shipping in the Persian Gulf. In early European trading, Brent crude is up 0.6% to $92.52 a barrel, while WTI futures rise 0.4% to $83.61 a barrel. The latest U.S. data showed crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels last week, while product stockpiles also increased. Despite the modest rebound, both benchmarks have fallen 15% so far this month as President Trump held off on renewed large-scale strikes against Iran. A broader retreat across commodity markets and a stronger U.S. dollar are also weighing on sentiment, creating additional headwinds. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
